To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) label smoothing can be generalized into a more general setting of using both positive and negative weights to combine the hard labels and soft labels; (ii) negative label smoothing (NLS) is more beneficial than positive label smoothing (PSL) when learning with noisy hard labels; (iii) the advantage of NLS vanishes when the label noise rate is low.

(1) $\textit{positive label smoothing}$ (PLS) and $\textit{Negative Label Smoothing}$ (NLS) are two different learning paradigms, (2) PLS is more beneficial when the training labels are clean, while NLS is more beneficial with noisy labels, and (3) PLS can be viewed as a regularization term that improves generalization, while NLS can be viewed to be a confidence regularization that helps in learning robust models.
